findings.where: Top of the page, at both widths: the area from the eyebrow 'Bali' through the h1 'Best Hostels in Canggu' and the lead paragraph
findings.fault: The page has no destination banner. It opens straight into a modest heading and body text on the plain sand ground, with no turquoise hero, no illustration, no big display type and no brand moment. The brief puts a destination page's top banner in the loud marketing zone. As built, the first screen looks like a plain document, the sterile look the brand names as its enemy.
findings.who_objects: The founder, because the brand's spine is 'loud moments, calm machine' and destination-page tops are named as a loud moment. Also the backpacker arriving from search, who wants to feel the place is worth a look. A flat text page about a surf town gives them no feeling and makes the brand look unfinished.

findings.where: 'What to look for' section, at both widths
findings.fault: This is the section that does half of the brief's job: what to look for in a Canggu hostel. Its heading is a small, uppercase, letter-spaced eyebrow, while the less important sections above it ('Surf', 'Vibe', 'Good for') get full-size headings. When you squint, it reads as a caption hanging off the tag wall rather than a section of its own. It also sits closer to the tags above it than the other sections sit to each other, which strengthens that reading.
findings.who_objects: The backpacker deciding on a hostel, who scans for the advice they can act on. The one section that gives it is the easiest to skim past.

findings.where: 'Good for' tags, at both widths (worst at phone, where they fill five rows)
findings.fault: Twelve tags of equal weight, from 'First-time surfers' to 'Sunsets', form the heaviest block on the page. They list everything as a fit and nothing as a poor fit, so they don't help a visitor judge whether Canggu suits them, which is the page's job. The wall looks busy and still says little. Taken together, the strongest signal reads as 'good for everyone'.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker weighing Canggu against Uluwatu or Lombok, who needs to know who it's wrong for (someone who wants quiet, someone who doesn't ride a scooter). Twelve undifferentiated positives read as marketing, not judgement. That undercuts a brand whose claim is honest, merit-only advice.

findings.where: Desktop, the whole body: the text column against the tag rows and the coming-soon notice
findings.fault: At desktop, the text sits in a narrow left column, about the left third of the frame, and the right two-thirds stay empty all the way down. The tag rows and the dark notice break out to the full content width, but the notice's text stays in the narrow column, so most of the dark box is empty on the right. With two different right edges and a mostly empty box, the arrangement looks unfinished rather than deliberately asymmetric.
findings.who_objects: A desktop visitor planning a trip, who sees a page that looks half-laid-out. Also the founder, since craft is the brand's promise over Hostelworld.

findings.where: First screen at both widths, and the coming-soon notice
findings.fault: Nothing above the fold says what MantaHostels is or why a visitor should use it rather than the sites they know. That first comes in the notice at the very end. The notice also promises to 'show direct-booking options alongside the major booking sites so you can compare and choose'. That reads as side-by-side price comparison with OTAs, which the project's own constraints bar Manta from showing.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor from search, who can't tell who is behind this guide or why to come back. Also the founder, because a launch promise the platform can't keep (price comparison against Hostelworld and Booking.com) costs trust when listings go live.

findings.where: Guide body: the 'Surf', 'Vibe' and 'What to look for' advice, at both widths
findings.fault: The guide carries no date or 'updated' line. In Canggu, venues, crowds and prices change from season to season, so the visitor can't tell whether the advice is current.
findings.who_objects: A backpacker relying on the guide to choose a base. Undated travel advice is easy to discount, and the site has no reviews or listings yet to lend it weight.
